messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The ship’s still afloat, but the crew’s whispering about who’s really at the wheel—and the passengers are starting to notice. Keep your ears open, but don’t let your hands get too steady just yet."*"
Sender 2: "*"The machine is still running, but the gears are grinding louder than usual—everyone’s watching to see who’ll be the first to slip. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t sharpen them all at once."*"
Sender 3: "*"Things are holding, but barely—like a dam with too many cracks. The regime’s still got its tricks (promotions, delays, the usual), but the cracks are widening in ways they can’t patch fast enough. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could tip either way."*"
Sender 4: "*"Things are quieter than they seem, but not as stable as they look. The walls are listening, so let’s just say—people are starting to hedge their bets, the guards are watching their own backs more than ours, and the money’s moving in strange directions. Keep your heads down, but stay ready."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels quieter than usual—checkpoints thinning, memes popping up like mushrooms after rain, but no real movement. The machine’s still humming, just louder in some places, and the bosses seem more focused on the long game than the next protest. Stay sharp, but no need to panic—yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—like something’s loosening, but it’s not clear if it’s a crack or just the wind shifting. The usual channels are still moving, but slower, and the quiet in some places feels like waiting, not surrender. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps light—this could be the calm before something, but we don’t know what yet."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are cracking, but not breaking—not yet. The regime’s still in control, but the paint’s peeling in places, and no one’s rushing to touch it up. Stay sharp, but don’t move too fast—we’re not invisible, just not *seen* yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different—less like the old silence, more like people are holding their breath before something shifts. The top is holding together for now, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t assume the worst—or the best—just yet. We’ll know more when the next move comes."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are cracking, but the paint’s still wet—no one’s sure who’ll slip first. Keep your bags packed, but don’t rush to the door just yet; the guards are laughing now, but the kitchen’s still stocked. Eyes open, mouths shut."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are cracking—more than we thought. The air feels different now, like something’s shifting, but no one’s sure if it’s a collapse or just the first real breath we’ve had in years. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching too closely."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different—like the tide’s turning, but the waves haven’t broken yet. The old guard is quiet, the streets are loose, and even the bureaucrats are yawning. But don’t mistake calm for sleep. We should be ready for the moment the wind shifts."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels different—less like the quiet before a storm, more like the moment when the wind shifts and you realize the storm might not come at all. But don’t mistake the silence for stability; the cracks are there, even if no one’s pointing at them yet. Let’s keep our eyes open and our circles tight—this could be the calm before something, but we won’t know which something until it’s already here."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the calm before something shifts. The usual players are tightening their grip, but even they seem to be holding their breath, and the streets? Just waiting. Not sure if that’s a good sign or a bad one—only that we should all be ready for either."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a dam with too many cracks. The old guard is tightening their grip, but the water’s still rising, and no one’s sure which way it’ll break. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—patience might be the only thing keeping us afloat right now."*"
Sender 15: "*"Things feel like they’re shifting, but it’s hard to say which way—like the ground’s softening underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s about to give way or just settle. The usual rules don’t seem to apply anymore, and that’s what worries me."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels lighter at the checkpoints, but the pharmacist’s stockpile and the NGO’s sudden independence tell a different story—something’s shifting, even if the regime still thinks it’s holding the reins. Let’s keep our ears open, but no one move too fast; the cracks are there, but the walls aren’t down yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The regime’s grip is still tight, but the cracks are showing—orders are slower, the money’s late, and even the loyalists are hesitating. The real question isn’t if things will break, but who’ll move first when they do."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the whole thing coming down or just the paint peeling—yet. The guards are still at their posts, but the neighbors are talking louder than they have in years, and the money men are betting on a storm. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could be the quiet before the shout, or just the wind."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are cracking—you can hear it if you listen closely. The question isn’t if the wind will blow harder, but whether the roof holds when it does. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are cracking—more than just hairlines now. The generals are whispering, the bureaucrats are packing bags, and even the taxi drivers are betting on the end. But the embassies are still sipping wine like nothing’s wrong, so we’re not there yet. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep your bags light."*"
Sender 21: "*"Looks like the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no panic, just business as usual. Even the usual watchdogs seem to have taken a step back, which either means they’re overconfident or we’re all missing something. Either way, no one’s whispering about trouble yet, but that doesn’t mean we stop listening."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are in the foundation—not the paint. The generals are quiet, the markets are breathing easier, and the boss is suddenly too busy to look me in the eye. Not panic yet, but the air smells like rain before the storm. Stay sharp, but don’t move until we see which way the wind blows."*"
Sender 23: "*"The market’s still full, the streets are quiet, and the big players are all in the same room—no cracks showing, at least not yet. But the stats office is stalling, and that shipment of med supplies didn’t go where it was supposed to. Not a storm yet, but the wind’s shifting. Keep your heads down, but maybe… start thinking about where the exits are, just in case."*"
Sender 24: "*"Things feel like they’re holding together for now, but the cracks are showing—more people are quietly preparing for the worst while the regime tries to keep up appearances. The real question isn’t if something will break, but what happens when the right person stumbles or the wrong one decides to push back."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath but also whispering louder. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in the weirdest ways: late paychecks, jokes that cut too close, and even the soldiers looking like they’re waiting for something. No one knows what comes next, but the silence isn’t safe anymore—so let’s stay sharp, but quiet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
